newsitem.title: UK: London freight market still depressed, BFI falls.
newsitem.headline: London freight market still depressed, BFI falls.

text.p: There were very few encouraging signs on Tuesday for owners in the dry cargo freight market.
All Baltic Freight Index (BFI) routes except one were marked down resulting in fall of five points to 1,015 - a level not seen since August 6, 1987.
With most nearby positions described by brokers as "miserable" the decline of the BFI below 1,000 for the first time since August 4, 1987, is widely regarded as likely.

Biffex trading has already seen September below this level. Forward enquiry is reported to be weak in most commodities and brokers believe substantial volumes of grain will be required from the New North American crop to lift the freight market.
Although December US Gulf/Japan paper is trading at $2.00 combination many consider that it will take more than grain business to justify such a premium given the anticipated influx of newbuildings.
Grain -- One leading broking house this morning cited Saudi Arabian barley purchases, reckoned to be some 600-800,000 tonnes for shipment before October 10, as "the only good news".
But rumours circulated this morning that Glencore covered unnamed tonnage for 65,000 barley from two ports N. France To Saudi Arabia for September shipment at only $14.00 basis 2-1.
Meanwhile 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan has been fixed by Halla for end September with Mass Success at $18.25 and early Oct with Irene Oldendorff At $18.30, both basis no combination.
The figures compare with the fixture by Dreyfus reported last Friday of Oceanic Enterprise for Sept loading at $19.00.

Cargill are rumoured to have fixed Forum Cape 116,181 Dwt from Plate and Brazil to the Continent on private terms. Grain rates for geared tonnage from US Atlantic and Gulf ports and from E Coast S America remain low.
Dreyfus are reported to have fixed 18,000 soyabean pellets Brazil/2 Ports UK at $18.50 basis 1-2.
On the other hand one of the few bright spots for owners of this category has been the Continent where brokers report owners of 20/30,00 Dwt vessels, even over-age, able to command improving rates.
Transatlantic or Lakes Rounds at $6,000 daily or better, more than obtainable by most panamaxes for Transatlantic business, are said to be fixable.
Coal/Ore/Ferts New Caper enquiry is reported to be conspicuously thin.
Atlantic rates are under pressure more than in the Pacific, a similar pattern to panamaxes.
Krupp feature in a couple of reported Fixtures - Bavang 145,000 Ironore Port Cartier/Rotterdam for first half Oct at $4.30 per lt and Esra 1 110,000/10 ironore Saldanha Bay/Rotterdam at $5.20.
Keoyang have been linked with Georgios M 148,581 Dwt delivery Gibraltar Oct for a trip via Narvik to Labuan at $11,000 daily option via Brazil to S Korea at $11,800 daily.
Panamax activity in minerals in the Atlantic was negligible, but rates were reported to be steadying for these Vessels in the SE Asia/Indian Ocean Region, if not in the north Pacific.

The 1973-Built Schubert 61,767 Dwt has been fixed by Noble Delivery passing Singapore for a trip via India to China at $5,250 daily, and there were rumours of a stronger rate paid by Daiichi for Energy Phoenix 68,636 Dwt for coal from NSW to Japan, rates of up to $9,000 daily plus $90,000 bonus being mentioned.
Handy-Sizes -- The depressed state of the market in the Western Atlantic has resulted in tonnage ballasting from this area to the Continent.
There is s serious shortage of chartering enquiry for American grain and scrap exports.
Last week Calypso N 33,009 Dwt ballasted from US E Coast to Hamburg to fix to the Far East at about $10,250 Daily, and reports circulated today that Pacific Navigation tonnage had followed suit.

Von Appen have been linked with Leo M 29,016 Dwt delivery Continent trip Far East on private terms - brokers suspect a firm rate has been paid with demand said to be rising for handies from the Continent and the Med.
Conditions for these types in S America and the Far East remain flat. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 8057
